To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
PKA phosphorylation or cTnI S23/24D phosphomimetic mutation weakens cTnI-troponin C interactions and reduces the Ca(2)-binding affinity of cTn.

PKA phosphorylation and phosphomimetic mutation of cardiac troponins I (cTni) alters the rate and extent of myofibrillar relaxation, and this is mediated by changes in the Ca2+ affinity of cTn and cTnI-troponin C (TnC) interactions.
PKA phosphorylation and phosphomimetic cTnI mutations weaken C-I interaction and alter thin filament activation and relaxation kinetics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of PKA phosphorylation in modulating thin filament activation and relaxation kinetics.
the molecular mechanisms underlying cardiac muscle contraction.
the molecular mechanisms of cardiac muscle contraction and relaxation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the phosphorylation of cMyBP-C by PKA is a major mechanism by which PKA regulates the Ca(2) sensitivity of the contractile system in ventricular myocytes, but the phosphorylation of other myofilament proteins (cTn and titin) also play a role.
PKA-mediated phosphorylations of myofilament proteins, particularly cTnI Ser23/24, are important modulators of the kinetics of myofilament activation and relaxation.
phosphorylation of cMyBP-C and cTnI are both important for β-adrengic regulation of cardiac function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

PKA phosphorylation modulates cardiac contractility via multiple mechanisms including: 1) increased Ca(2+) affinity of troponin C, 2) decreased Ca(2+) activation of myosin ATPase, and 3) decreased C-I interaction, which may contribute to the slowing of thin filament activation.
phosphorylation of cMyBP-C and cTnI by PKA, and possibly titin, can alter the Ca(2+)/myosin interaction and myofilament cross-bridge kinetics.

phosphorylation of cMyBP-C, cTnI and titin by PKA results in increased thin filament Ca(2+) affinity, increased thin filament activation rate, decreased thin filament relaxation kinetics and decreased Ca(2+) cooperativity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
phosphorylation of cMyBP-C by PKA, and phosphorylation of cTroponin I, have opposing effects on the rate of myofilament relaxation.
PKA phosphorylation can modulate the kinetics of myofilament activation and relaxation.
PKA phosphorylation modulates thin filament activation and relaxation kinetics, and these effects can be explained by weakened C-I interaction.
